Operating Characteristics of the iBOIN Design

Source: R/sim_iboin.R
sim_iboin.Rd

Simulate trials of the iBOIN design of Zhou et al. (2021), which brings prior information on the DLT probability of every dose into the BOIN design, and summarize how often each dose is selected as the MTD and how the patients are distributed over the doses.

Usage

sim_iboin(
  target,
  p_true,
  skeleton,
  prior_ess,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = 18,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  robust = FALSE,
  select_with_prior = TRUE,
  min_mtd_sample = 1,
  overdose_cutoff = NULL,
  n_earlystop_rule = c("with_stay", "simple"),
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, for example 0.30.

p_true

Numeric vector. True DLT probability at each dose level, in increasing dose order.

skeleton

Numeric vector, one value per dose. Prior DLT probability at each dose, strictly between 0 and 1.

prior_ess

Whole number or vector of whole numbers, one per dose. Prior effective sample size. See iboin_boundary.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at the current dose and the design would stay there. Defaults to 18. The simulations of the article do not stop early; a value above the maximum sample size switches the rule off.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. Posterior probability cutoff for dose elimination. Defaults to 0.95.

extrasafe

Logical scalar. Apply the stricter safety stopping rule at the lowest dose. Defaults to FALSE.

offset

Numeric scalar between 0 and 0.5. Amount by which cutoff_eli is relaxed for the safety stopping rule. Defaults to 0.05.

robust

Logical scalar. Use the robust prior, which drops the prior information above the prior MTD when the prior MTD lies in the upper half of the doses. Defaults to FALSE. See iboin_boundary.

select_with_prior

Logical scalar. Add the prior information to the estimates of the DLT probabilities from which the MTD is selected, as iboin_select_mtd does. Defaults to TRUE, which reproduces the operating characteristics of the article. With FALSE the MTD is selected from the data alone, by boin_select_mtd.

min_mtd_sample

Integer scalar. Smallest number of patients a dose must have been given to be selected as the MTD. Defaults to 1.

overdose_cutoff

Numeric scalar or NULL. Doses with a true DLT probability above this value count as overdoses in the summary. Defaults to NULL, the target.

n_earlystop_rule

Character scalar, either "with_stay" or "simple". Under "with_stay" the trial stops at n_earlystop only when the design would remain at the current dose. Under "simple" it stops as soon as the threshold is reached.

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the trial level data in the result. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Report the progress in messages. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class c("iboin_oc", "boin_oc"), a list with the components of the result of sim_boin and in addition

design

The name of the design, "iBOIN".

skeleton

The skeleton.

prior_ess

The prior effective sample sizes used, after the robust prior has been applied.

select_with_prior

Whether the selection of the MTD used the prior information.

boundary

The iboin_boundary object used.

The components lambda_e and lambda_d are the boundaries of the BOIN design, which the iBOIN boundaries approach as patients are treated at a dose.

Details

The trials are simulated by iboin_simulate with the boundaries of iboin_boundary. The article gives two ways to select the MTD at the end of the trial, with and without the prior information in the estimates of the DLT probabilities, and does not say which one its simulation study uses. Its operating characteristics are reproduced with the prior information (see inst/reproduce/reproduce_Zhou2021.R), which is therefore the default. The selection from the data alone (select_with_prior = FALSE) keeps a misspecified prior from biasing the selection, at the price of a lower probability of selecting the true MTD when the prior is right.

With a prior effective sample size of 0 at every dose the result is, for the same seed, that of sim_boin.

The result can be passed to oc_results and oc_compare, where it appears under the name iBOIN.

References

Zhou, Y., Lee, J. J., Wang, S., Bailey, S. and Yuan, Y. (2021). Incorporating historical information to improve phase I clinical trials. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 20, 1017-1034. doi:10.1002/pst.2121

See also

iboin_boundary, iboin_simulate, sim_iboin_multi, sim_boin

Examples

# Scenario 3 of Zhou et al. (2021): the prior MTD is the true MTD
oc <- sim_iboin(
  target = 0.30,
  p_true = c(0.08, 0.15, 0.31, 0.45, 0.55),
  skeleton = c(0.10, 0.19, 0.30, 0.42, 0.54),
  prior_ess = 3,
  n_cohort = 10,
  cohort_size = 3,
  n_earlystop = 100,
  n_trials = 500,
  seed = 123
)
oc
#> iBOIN operating characteristics
#>   target DLT rate : 0.3
#>   trials          : 500
#>   cohorts         : 10 of size 3
#>   max sample size : 30
#>   skeleton        : 0.10 0.19 0.30 0.42 0.54
#>   prior ESS       : 3 3 3 3 3
#> 
#>                   DL1  DL2  DL3  DL4  DL5 Total / No MTD
#> True DLT rate (%) 8.0 15.0 31.0 45.0 55.0               
#> MTD selected (%)  1.6 23.8 62.2 12.0  0.2            0.2
#> Patients treated  3.8  9.4 12.8  3.6  0.4           29.9
#> Patients with DLT 0.3  1.5  4.0  1.7  0.2            7.6
#> 
#> Doses above a true DLT rate of 0.3: DL3, DL4, DL5
#>   Patients treated there              : 55.7%
#>   Trials treating any patient there   : 95.6%
#>   Trials treating over 60% there      : 47.2%
#>   Trials treating over 80% there      : 0%
#>   Trials selecting an MTD there       : 74.4%
